diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the transition function $\rho=\chi_K$; i.e. the indicative function of $K$, then the H-limit of the concurrent coefficient $b^\varepsilon$ is exactly the effective matrix $A$.

issues.failure_explanation: The energy-limit steps use $(1-\rho)\varphi\phi^\varepsilon$ and $\varphi\rho\psi^\varepsilon$ as test functions. This requires $\nabla\rho$ and $\partial_t\rho$ to exist and be bounded, so that the test functions lie in $L^2(0,T;H_0^1)$ and the time-derivative pairing can be integrated by parts. No regularity of $\rho$ is assumed. The immediately following remark applies the bound to the discontinuous $\rho=\chi_K$, which the argument does not cover.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume $\rho\in W^{1,\infty}(D_T)$ in the proposition. Treat $\rho=\chi_K$ separately via locality of H-convergence (or an $L^1$-stability argument for H-limits).
issues.overall_effect: The proposition and its corollary are proved only for Lipschitz (in $x,t$) transition functions. The remark for $\rho=\chi_K$ is not justified by the given proof.
issues.title: H-limit bound proof differentiates the transition function, which is not assumed smooth
issues.why_classification: A standard regularity hypothesis plus a standard locality argument restores all stated conclusions. The later error analysis does not use this proposition.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict to symmetric $a^\varepsilon$ and $A_H$ (hence symmetric $b^\varepsilon_H$) in Lemma lem:added-1 and Theorem thm:global. Alternatively, supply a different $H^1$-stability argument for nonsymmetric coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: For nonsymmetric $a^\varepsilon$ or $A_H$, the bound (sta2) is unsupported. Via (sta4), so are the $H^1$ estimate (thm12) and the time-derivative estimate (thm13). The latter feeds the local estimate in Remark rmk:local.
issues.title: H^1-stability (sta2) uses a telescoping identity valid only for symmetric coefficients
issues.why_classification: The rates survive for symmetric coefficients, but the nonsymmetric part of the advertised class $\mathcal M$ is lost unless a genuinely new stability argument is provided.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An interesting finding in Theorem~\ref{thm:local} suggests that the pollution of the local energy error may be reduced if we take $\rho$ as the indicator function of $K$.
which has been confirmed both theoretically and experimentally

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that taking $\rho=\chi_K$ eliminates the factor $|K\setminus K_0|^{1/2-1/p}$ and reduces local pollution. It also claims local accuracy is confirmed theoretically. However, bounding the remaining terms of Theorem thm:local in Remark rmk:local reintroduces $|K|^{1/2-1/p}(\|u^\varepsilon\|_{L^p}+\|\nabla u^\varepsilon\|_{L^p}+\dots)$, with the larger set $K$ and an extra $d^{-1}$. The final local bound therefore contains $d^{-1}|K|^{1/2-1/p}$, which is independent of $h,H,\Delta t$. Since $|K|\gtrsim d^n$, this term does not vanish under refinement and in 2D grows as $d\to0$. No convergence of the local energy error, and no improvement over the $\rho\neq\chi_K$ case, is established.

failure_location.quote: This factor can be eliminated by choosing $\rho=\chi_K$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the elimination and theoretical-confirmation claims and state that the final local bound retains a non-vanishing $d^{-1}|K|^{1/2-1/p}$ term. Alternatively, prove homogenization-rate bounds for $\|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^2(K)}$ and $\|\partial_t(u^\varepsilon-u)\|_{H^{-1}(K)}$ under additional structure.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised elimination/reduction of the Meyers-type pollution and the claimed theoretical confirmation of microscopic accuracy (abstract, introduction, conclusion) are unsupported. The local estimate is only an $O(1)$ modelling-error bound.
issues.title: Claimed elimination of Meyers factor and theoretical confirmation of local accuracy not supported
issues.why_classification: The formal theorems stand, but a substantive advertised promise about the local error must be withdrawn or replaced by a new, contained homogenization-rate argument.
